hlni.insight: Academic difficulty is a function of subject-interest alignment rather than degree title.
hlni.audienceGap: Students often assume one degree is inherently harder or superior to the other.
hlni.viewerChange: Shifts focus from degree hierarchy to personal curiosity and analytical lens.
hlni.support: Foundational business concepts are universal; degrees are just different frameworks for application.
hlni.payoff: The hierarchy myth is dismantled, encouraging the student to choose based on their specific analytical preference.

shots.name: The Challenge
shots.visual: Split screen. Left: B.Com label. Right: BBA label. A floating text appears: 'Analyze a business failure'.
shots.dialogue: Which degree tackles this problem? B.Com or BBA?
shots.cameraPerformance: Static, focused on the floating text.

shots.name: The Reveal
shots.visual: Both labels light up. Two icons appear: a magnifying glass (B.Com) and a strategist hat (BBA).
shots.dialogue: Both. One explores the accounting trail. The other, the management strategy.

shots.name: The Insight
shots.visual: Host looking at camera, leaning in.
shots.dialogue: It's not about which is harder. It's about where you want to look. Match your curiosity, not the labels.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a shared business problem to show that both degrees cover common ground but through different lenses.

selected.title: The Syllabus Guessing Game
selected.audienceGap: Belief that one degree is inherently 'harder' than the other.
selected.hlni: Academic difficulty is often a function of 'subject-interest alignment' rather than degree title.
selected.viewerChange: Challenges the perception of degree hierarchy.
selected.concept: An interactive puzzle asking the viewer to guess which degree a specific learning outcome belongs to.
selected.device: Rapid-fire visual reveal that both degrees cover similar 'foundational' ground.
selected.support: Foundational business topics are universal; the differentiation is in the application context.
methodSteps: Ask the audience: 'Which degree solves this?'
selected.interpretationRule: If both solve the problem, the difference is the lens (e.g., efficiency vs. growth).
selected.visibleProof: The viewer sees the same business problem solved through two different, equally valid lenses.
selected.payoff: The hierarchy myth is dismantled, encouraging deeper research.
